common.title: Parliamentary video, documented.
common.lede: Find official parliamentary video from around the world.
common.methodTitle: Technical access and provider terms are different questions.
common.methodCopy: Technically validated public direct feeds play here unless recorded terms expressly prohibit third-party reuse. A play button is not a licence; source owners can request removal.
common.footer: Parliament Streams is an independent research catalogue.
common.openVideoCopy: Open parliamentary video requires direct, interoperable streams such as HLS, with clear terms that permit embedding, rebroadcasting, preservation, and independent monitoring.
common.openStreamsCopy: Open parliamentary video also needs open schedule data. Legislatures should publish timely, machine-readable programme and event feeds at stable URLs, with clear reuse terms, persistent identifiers, time zones, and prompt corrections.
common.accessNeedsReviewDescription: Technical access needs review or the latest check was not clean.
common.accessLinkOnlyDescription: No native playback URL is recorded; use the official page.
common.useExplicitDescription: Reuse appears permitted under recorded source conditions.
common.useEmbedOnlyDescription: Use the official provider or institutional embed only.
common.useNoThirdPartyDescription: Recorded terms require link-out or separate permission.
common.usePersonalPendingDescription: Public terms do not yet clearly support third-party use.
common.useNoncommercialPendingDescription: Some non-commercial use is documented, but full-stream playback still needs clarification.
common.sourcePlayableDescription: The source can play directly in this catalogue.
common.sourceLinkOutDescription: Use the official site because playback is not embedded here.
common.sourceFallbackDescription: The catalogue can hand off to an official provider embed or fallback surface.
common.sourceResearchDescription: Viewing is not enabled here. The details show the recorded reason and remaining checks.
common.viewingFeedUnverified: This specific feed has not passed playback checks.
common.viewingSourceUnresolved: The stream provider, terms and playback support still need review.
common.ready: Ready to load the official feed
common.disabled: Playback is not enabled for this source
common.optOutPlaybackPolicy: This public endpoint is playable under the catalogue’s opt-out policy. This is not a licence; review the source notes and report concerns for prompt removal.
common.youtubePlaybackPolicy: Playback uses the provider’s official privacy-enhanced embed; no stream manifest is extracted.

institutions.title: Legislatures
institutions.lede: Entries identify legislative bodies and chambers for research. Inclusion does not validate a stream; see the catalogue for viewing sources.
institutions.scopeCopy: Our current research covers 71 country groups from the EIU Democracy Index 2024 baseline, including first-level and autonomous special-status legislatures. Chambers and distinct legislative organs are listed within their institutions where applicable. This is a working inventory; completeness and viewing-service validation remain separate.
institutions.contributeCopy: Missing an institution or an official broadcast? Have a correction, translation, accessibility finding or another idea? Contributions of any size are welcome.
institutions.loadError: The institution list could not be loaded.
institutions.nameNote: Institution names follow the source records; research notes are available in English.
institutions.noServiceNote: No documented viewing source is a research gap; it does not establish that the institution has no broadcasts.
institutions.searchHint: Country searches include regional institutions and associated territories.

project.title: Data and methods
project.intro: An open source project documenting legislatures, official broadcasts and programme data.
project.inventoryCopy: Bodies and chambers, with evidence about legislative authority and research scope. A body record does not establish an available broadcast.
project.catalogueCopy: Official viewing sources linked to those institutions. A source can be an external page, an archive or an in-page player.
project.reviewCopy: Technical access, identity, feed mapping and reuse rights are separate findings. Automation proposes changes for human review; it does not automatically admit sources.
project.productsCopy: Reviewed records generate these pages and files. Programme timestamps are stored in UTC and displayed in the viewer’s local timezone.
project.cadence: Inventory and catalogue changes are reviewed and committed. Schedules and exports refresh every six hours.
project.coverage: Guide coverage is partial. “Automated schedules” counts sources connected to an implemented parser, not populated guides. Event listings and XMLTV coverage are separate; XMLTV requires a reviewed exact feed mapping and complete times. Collection errors are different from a confirmed empty listing window.
project.rights: Project code licensing is separate from broadcast and source-data rights. Check each source’s conditions; no blanket licence is asserted for third-party material.
project.contributeCopy: Help with sources, research, metadata, programme guides, translations, accessibility, documentation or code.
project.inventoryInclusion: Legislative authority must be supported by evidence. Ordinary municipal and advisory bodies are excluded; unresolved authority cases stay marked. A viewing source is not required for the inventory.
project.catalogueInclusion: Requires an identified official source of legislative video or audio, live or recorded. Unusable or research-only viewing routes stay outside the catalogue. Sources beyond the inventory’s research priorities can qualify; embedding and reuse are reviewed separately.
project.scheduleInclusion: Official calendars remain useful links even without a collector. Automated listings need structured source data with explicit dates and times; missing times are not invented. XMLTV also needs a reviewed exact feed mapping and credible programme start and end times.
project.supportingCopy: Maintained inputs, review decisions and dated evidence complement the public outputs. These records do not certify a working stream or grant reuse rights.
project.methodChecks: Researchers reconcile official institutions and source ownership, then record identity, technical access, accessibility and rights as separate findings. Automated checks propose changes for human review; dated reports preserve what was actually checked.
project.methodSchedules: Collectors distinguish empty listings from failed requests and mark retained data as stale. Source timezones are normalized to UTC; the website displays your local time. A meeting calendar is not automatically a television programme guide.
project.colophonBuild: A static HTML, CSS and JavaScript site, built from maintained data with Python tools and published through GitHub Actions and GitHub Pages. D3 draws the map; HLS.js supports compatible video playback. Headings use Georgia with system-font fallbacks.
project.colophonPrivacy: No accounts, project analytics or stream proxy. Interface language is stored locally in your browser. Choosing playback can contact the official broadcaster or provider, whose privacy terms also apply.
project.colophonCredits: Project code uses the BSD 3-Clause licence. Images, flags, maps, icons and bundled libraries retain their own credits and licences. Broadcast and source-data rights are separate.

iptv.title: Use in an IPTV app
iptv.intro: Paste a playlist URL into your player. Add the XMLTV URL as its guide / EPG.
iptv.note: Includes continuous channels and streams available only during sittings or events. Some may be offline between proceedings. Guide coverage is partial; some channels have no listings.
iptv.failed: Copy unavailable. The URL is selected for you to copy manually.
iptv.filterScope: These playlists are global; page filters do not change them.
iptv.vlcOpen: In VLC, choose Media → Open Network Stream (Windows/Linux) or File → Open Network (macOS).
iptv.vlcPlay: Paste the URL, choose Play or Open, then select a channel in VLC’s playlist.
iptv.vlcGuide: Use the playlist URL for VLC playback. The XMLTV URL is a separate guide feed for apps that support XMLTV; these VLC steps do not configure an XMLTV guide.
